basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Defines what may be asked and how, not the responses or the people who answered.
Keeps wording, language, mode, order and routing explicit because each can change meaning.
Differs from a study or campaign, which uses the instrument in a sample and time.
Differs from a form in software, which may collect data without a measurement purpose.

may: Compose and version questions, modules and routing.
Check routing logic and validation rules for errors.
Prepare translations and accessible variants as drafts.
Map questions to concepts and variables.
mustNot: Publish or field an instrument without approval.
Change wording in a released version.
Add questions on sensitive topics without review.
requiresHuman: Approving consent text and sensitive questions.

considerations: Questions can intrude on privacy and cause distress, especially on health, sexuality or trauma.
Leading or biased wording distorts results used for policy.
Accessibility and language choices decide who can take part.
affectedParties: Researchers and agencies using the data

items: An instrument names questions, response options, routing, language and a version.
Often confused with the responses dataset, a survey campaign, a sample or an online form tool.
Comparability broken by unnoticed wording changes.
ISO 20252 market, opinion and social research.
HL7 FHIR R5 Questionnaire and QuestionnaireResponse.
